title: The Shadow and the Body
english: … Since, then, the ordinances of the law are the shadow, what is the body? What belongs to Christ is not shadow. So once the body has come, the shadow is superfluous.

On Colossians 2:18: What sort of humility? The humility of saying: “We are lowly, and God is great, too great to be served by us. Since we cannot reach as far as him, we win his favour through his angels, and through them we are brought to him.” Earlier he said, “who is the head of every rule and authority” (Colossians 2:10), and now he says: why do you go to the elements and to angels, abandoning their head, which is Christ?
The second catena form adds: … God is incomprehensible and invisible … since we cannot take in the Great One … And this is what he calls humility.

On Colossians 2:19: Here he made plain the aim we have been speaking of: what moved him to write was that some people were urging others to approach God through angels. We must, he says, hold fast to the head, for God the Word is the head of the universe. Why, then, let go of the head and cling to the body? The power of the angels may serve as a joint that links two or more limbs, but the benefit still comes to all from the head: to angels as angels, to archangels as archangels, to visible things as visible things. Picture the heaven as the head of the world and the sun and moon as its eyes. Arrange each part of the world in this way, as limbs in their order, and you will find one body of the universe. As there is a soul in the body and the body belongs to the soul, so you will find the invisible powers in the visible things. But the head is more sovereign than all of these, and from it the benefit flows into the whole body, supplied, of course, from the head.

title: False Asceticism and the Flesh
english: … this world or to live as its citizens, why do you put up with people who lay down rules for you by the standards of this world, as if you lived by them? Why, as though you were living in the world, do you submit to rules: “Do not taste, do not touch, do not handle”, things which all perish as they are used? He presents these as Greek doctrines, for in their error these people command that no one should touch or taste anything that has life. Yet all these things were given to human beings to be used up, that is, to be spent and consumed in the use and the needs of life. So “do not touch” what God has given is a rule “according to their commandments and their teachings”.

On Colossians 2:23: This means: be wary of these rules, I mean “do not handle, do not taste, do not touch”, which seem to make some sense, because abstaining from foods and refusing to pamper one’s own flesh with plenty is the mark of people who are humble-minded and do not spare the body. But although self-control is a fine thing, their second motive is impious. They abstain not only as people who have mastered the belly, but also as people who think they must not harm living creatures, which were given to be used up in the course of life. They want to be more merciful to the dumb animals than God is.
On Colossians 3:3: “Our life is hidden” stands for the blessedness of eternal life, which will be revealed to all when the glory of Christ is also revealed at his second coming.
On Colossians 3:5: Just as he often calls sin “flesh”, so now, listing the members of the flesh, he names fornication, uncleanness and the rest; for these are the members of sin.
On Colossians 3:9–10: By “the old man” he means the mind set on sin, and by its members, evil deeds; by “the new man” he means the spiritual mind, and by its members, good deeds.

title: The New Man and the Rule of Love
english: … members. And having listed the man made up of these members, he urges them to strip off the old man with his deeds. … As there is an old man, so there is a new one too, that is, the spiritual mind; and its members are good deeds, which he also lists when he says “kindness, long-suffering” and the rest (Colossians 3:12).

On Colossians 3:11: This is like the words “that he may be all in all” (1 Corinthians 15:28). What he means is this: that God may work all things in all who set their minds on the things of God. When you think and do what belongs to Christ, he is the one acting through you, and he is in you.
The second catena form adds: … not heaven in heaven, nor earth in earth. … He is in you by your doing what pleases him.

On Colossians 3:14: Unless love leads the way, none of our duties is carried through to completion. It is when we love one another that we both keep from harming one another and take care to do one another good.

On Colossians 3:15: Do not let those who lead you astray, he says, rob you of the prize; let the peace of Christ be the umpire among you, so that you are united to Christ. “And be thankful.” To whom? To Christ, of course, who called you; and do not run to angels for shelter.
The second catena form adds: … in your hearts, that is, by being united to Christ and setting your minds on what is his. Then comes another exhortation.
On Colossians 4:1: Since your slaves, he says, serve you with goodwill, you masters must also repay them justly and fairly, with the care that is fitting. So fairness answers to their goodwill.
